title: MingCute Screenshot Quality Recovery batch 082
review_goal: Differentiate save, scan, and scissors variants with screenshot grounded depicts and deterministic evidence fields.

items.depicts_observation: Floppy disk with one top notch window and one lower rectangular label area
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants the classic floppy disk metaphor instead of a document confirmation symbol.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the checked page variant when the save state should read like a completed file rather than disk media.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot is clearly a floppy disk body with a top notch and lower label panel.

items.depicts_observation: Four open corner brackets forming one square scan frame with no center mark
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a camera style scan frame built only from corner brackets.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the circular scan variant when the mark should look like a ring with a sweeping diagonal segment.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot is made from four corner brackets and does not include the circular ring seen in the other scan variant.

items.depicts_observation: Open circular ring with a diagonal sweep cutting across the upper right side
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants scanning to feel like a circular sweep instead of corner brackets around a frame.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the corner frame scan when the mark should be four separated brackets with an empty center.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot wraps the scan idea into a ring and diagonal sweep rather than a square bracket frame.

items.depicts_observation: Open scissors with two round finger loops below and crossing blades pointing upward
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants the familiar vertical scissors pose with loops at the bottom and blades above.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the sideways or rotated scissors when the tool should not read as the standard upright cutting pose.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot follows the classic scissors arrangement with the handles below and the crossed blades rising above them.

items.depicts_observation: Rotated scissors with one handle loop hanging lower left and one blade shooting upward past the crossing point
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a more dynamic rotated scissors silhouette instead of the straight upright tool pose.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the classic upright scissors or the sideways scissors where the cutting tool should face in a more stable orientation.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot tilts the scissors and exaggerates one upward blade instead of the balanced upright form.
